svg.title: Japan at a glance — one-page infographic
svg.desc: Editorial infographic: stylized map of Japan with its four largest cities, a country overview, nominal GDP 2015–2024 bar chart, population composition donut chart, and travel highlights.

g.text: AN ISLAND NATION IN EAST ASIA
Geography, people, economy and travel — one country on a single page.

g.text: Largest cities by city-proper population · double ring marks the capital

text.tspan: Japan is an archipelago of roughly 14,000 islands strung
along the Pacific Ring of Fire. Four of them — Honshu,
Hokkaido, Kyushu and Shikoku — hold nearly all of its
124 million people. With mountains covering about three
quarters of the land, life crowds onto narrow coastal
plains, above all the Tokyo–Osaka corridor, home to the
planet's largest metropolitan area. A constitutional
monarchy with the world's oldest royal line, Japan pairs
deep tradition — shrines, tea and sumo — with hyper-modern
cities stitched together by punctual shinkansen trains.
From snow festivals in Hokkaido to subtropical beaches in Okinawa, Japan compresses striking
variety into a country smaller than California. Having urbanized, industrialized and aged earlier
than most, it now offers a preview of a wealthy, super-aged society that still runs with precision.
Japan runs the world's fourth-largest economy
and remains a manufacturing power behind
global names in cars, machinery, robotics
and gaming — Toyota, Sony and Nintendo
among them — while services now generate
about 70% of output. Measured in dollars,
GDP has drifted sideways for a decade: real
growth is positive but slow, and a sharply
weaker yen since 2022 has shrunk its dollar
value even as domestic activity expanded.

g.text: Donut slivers expanded to readable width · by nationality, 2023
Neon Shibuya, old Asakusa — and more Michelin stars than any other city.
The old capital — 1,600 temples, Fushimi Inari's gates, historic Gion.
Japan's kitchen: Dotonbori street food, takoyaki stalls, a grand castle.
A moving Peace Memorial, then Itsukushima's 'floating' torii offshore.
The 3,776 m icon, best seen from Hakone's lakes, ropeways and onsen.
Powder snow in Niseko, lavender fields in Furano, Sapporo's miso ramen.
Sources: World Bank & IMF (nominal GDP, current US$) · Statistics Bureau of Japan / Immigration Services Agency, 2023–24 residency data · GSI island survey, 2023.
Population shares reflect nationality; the census does not record ethnicity. Figures rounded; map stylized, not to scale. One static SVG — no scripts or raster images.
